trust_decision.summary: Attaching a related record to a parent record must pass the parent resource field's attach_<field>? policy; at the pinned commit that policy ran only when the attach form was rendered (associations#new) and not when the form was submitted (associations#create), which writes the association in create_association.

landing_point.why: the attach authorization before_action is scoped to :new only, while create (line 89) performs the association write with no field-level check

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The create-through-association path is a different feature (creating a record under a parent, governed by create?/create_<field>? on the new child), and the update path is ordinary record editing under update?, so a solver can argue attach_<field>? was never meant to cover them; the advisory names the attach endpoint.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Detach and association browsing must keep working under their own policies (detach_<field>? evaluated on the attachment record, view_<field>? on the parent); a blanket attach before_action, or one that keys on @attachment_record instead of the parent record, breaks legitimate detach/index and contradicts the parent-record semantics used by the UI gate

O6_input_shapes: association kinds has_many / has_many-through / has_one / HABTM / array (the fix is a shape-agnostic before_action)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: POST /resources/:resource_name with via_record_id + via_relation + via_relation_class links the newly created record into the parent's association (FK assignment for belongs_to/has_many, << for through/HABTM) with no attach_<field>? (nor create_<field>?) check on the parent resource
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: it is the create feature, authorized by create? on the new child, and the parent association is populated as a side effect; the advisory names the attach endpoint
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package, one controller file away from the landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: PATCH /resources/:resource_name/:id with a belongs_to foreign key (or fields[related_id]) re-points an existing record's relationship with only update? on that record
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: editing a record's own belongs_to field is the update feature and is gated by update?, not by the association attach policy
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the other uncovered route, one directory from the landing point

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second, controller-level association writer that links new records into a parent association without any field-level policy
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the framework already writes associations in two controllers (associations_controller.rb:104-106 and base_controller.rb:159); the create flow grew organically and has no policy hook

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a bulk-attach or for_attribute-keyed variant whose policy name comes from the association name while the check uses the field id
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: for_attribute is a supported option with a live example in the dummy app (spec/dummy/app/avo/resources/project.rb:95: even_reviews -> reviews) and the UI gate already keys on the association name (lib/avo/concerns/checks_assoc_authorization.rb:35)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an action that mutates associations in bulk (record.projects.clear) with no field-level authorization
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Avo actions receive a query and call model methods directly; the dummy app already ships one that rewrites an association

O9_family: missing authorization / improper access control (CWE-862, CWE-863, CWE-639)

O10_build.toolchain: Ruby 3.3.1, Bundler, Rails >= 8.0, RSpec (spec/dummy Rails app); yarn/esbuild + tailwind for assets (package.json:8-19)
O10_build.project_tests: request specs live in spec/requests and CI runs spec/features + spec/requests against a postgres service with yarn-built assets (.github/workflows/feature-tests.yml:50-103); the attach UI flow is covered by spec/system/avo/associations_using_fields_api_spec.rb:10-33, and spec/requests/avo/attachments_request_spec.rb:29-50 shows the house style of stubbing Avo::Services::AuthorizationService#authorize_action; system specs need headless Chrome via cuprite (spec/rails_helper.rb:15,127); no test exercises attach authorization because authorization_enabled? requires the avo-pro plugin (lib/avo/configuration.rb:148-150) and the dummy app ships no policies. The published diff adds no tests (fix.diff:5-17).

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: add :create to the existing authorize_attach_action before_action and stop, without touching the create-through route in base_controller or noticing that the policy key is the field id, not the association name

out_of_scope_notes: app/controllers/avo/attachments_controller.rb:9-29 (POST /avo/avo_api/resources/:resource_name/:id/attachments, config/routes.rb:15) attaches ActiveStorage files under a different policy namespace (upload_<attachment>?), outside this advisory's protection; not pursued.
app/controllers/avo/media_library_controller.rb with GET /attach-media (config/routes.rb:8) is a separate media-library upload sink; not pursued.
unverified: repo_mb could not be measured without a shell; the tree has 1470 tracked files including a full dummy Rails app, so it is clearly not a tiny repo.

The second uncovered route (PATCH ... belongs_to FK) is the weaker of the two; whether Avo intends attach_<field>? to cover plain field updates cannot be confirmed because the pinned tree has no docs/ directory.

Whether a hidden behavioural test can reach attach_<field>? at all depends on enabling authorization: authorization_enabled? is false in the open-source repo without the avo-pro plugin (lib/avo/configuration.rb:148-150), so a test must register a fake avo-pro plugin or stub the config as well as the authorization service.
present_in_latest is unknown for both O8 routes: no later release or latest code location was supplied ('none').
